overview: The CC Energy & Environment Committee approved its previous minutes, received updates on municipal energy programs, and discussed several community environmental campaigns, including a survey on restaurant takeout containers, Earth Month events, and a fossil fuel divestment proposal.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee voted to approve the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Administrative Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike announced a meeting with the Mayor scheduled for April 2nd, posted job openings for a housing planner and summer interns, and discussed technical issues affecting the committee's mailing list.

items.title: Single-Use Plastic Takeout Containers Project
items.summary: Lois Grossman and Benji presented a survey plan to gather information on container usage and cost differentials from Medford restaurants to help eliminate black plastic and transition to sustainable alternatives.

items.title: Municipal Energy Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike provided updates on Electrify Medford coaching, school HVAC upgrades, a newly secured municipal electricity contract, Green Score zoning recommendations, and state EV charging grants.

items.title: Reforestation and Tree Initiatives
items.summary: Lauretta James shared updates on Trees Medford programs and advocated for contacting state legislators to support bond funding for the Municipal Reforestation Bill.

items.title: Earth Month and Free Flea Market Events
items.summary: Prabita detailed plans for a daily social media campaign during Earth Month and a cooperative "free flea market" event with Tufts University scheduled for early May.

items.title: Fossil Fuel Divestment Proposal
items.summary: Josh Ekhart-Lee introduced a proposal to develop an ordinance directing the city treasurer to divest municipal funds from fossil fuels and other socially irresponsible industries.

items.title: New Business and Mayor's Meeting Preparation
items.summary: The committee discussed a potential dark skies ordinance presentation, state rodenticide bills, and preparation for their upcoming meeting with the Mayor.
